title: My preventive care
subtitle: Vaccines, check-ups and screening tests recommended for you by India's national health programmes.

when.closed: Last day was {{date}}. Ask your health worker.

reason.vBcg: Protects against severe forms of tuberculosis.
reason.vHepb: Protects the newborn from hepatitis B. Given within 24 hours of birth.
reason.vPenta: Protects against diphtheria, whooping cough, tetanus, hepatitis B and Hib.
reason.vRvv: Protects against severe diarrhoea caused by rotavirus.
reason.vFipv: An injection that adds protection against polio.
reason.vPcv: Protects against pneumonia caused by pneumococcus.
reason.vDpt: Booster against diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus.
reason.vVita: Vitamin A keeps the eyes healthy and helps fight infections.
reason.vTdPregnancy: Protects you and your newborn baby from tetanus.
reason.selfReported: You told us this was given; a health worker will confirm it.
reason.anc1: Register the pregnancy and have the first check-up by week {{to}}.
reason.anc2: Recommended between week {{from}} and week {{to}} of pregnancy.
reason.anc3: Recommended between week {{from}} and week {{to}} of pregnancy.
reason.folicAcid: One tablet a day in the first 3 months helps the baby's brain and spine grow.
reason.ifaPregnancy: One red iron tablet every day from the 4th month, for at least 180 days, prevents anaemia. Continue until {{until}}.
reason.calcium: Calcium tablets twice a day from the 4th month help protect against high BP in pregnancy. Continue until {{until}}.
reason.albendazolePregnancy: One deworming tablet in the middle three months of pregnancy.
reason.ultrasound: A scan in the middle of pregnancy checks the baby's growth.
reason.hbPregnancy: Hb is checked at every pregnancy check-up to find anaemia early.
reason.pmsma: Free check-up by a doctor at a government health centre on the 9th of every month.
reason.birthPlan: Your due date is around {{edd}}. Decide the hospital, the transport (call 108 or 102) and who will go with you. Delivery is free at government hospitals.
reason.hbnc: The ASHA visits the baby at home on day {{day}} to check feeding, warmth and danger signs.
reason.growthMonthly: Weigh the child every month until 3 years of age.
reason.growthQuarterly: Weigh the child every 3 months from 3 to 6 years.
reason.rbskAnganwadi: A health team checks children at the anganwadi twice a year.
reason.rbskSchool: A health team checks children at school once a year.
reason.dewormingHalf: Half a deworming tablet (200 mg) on National Deworming Day. Next: {{next}}.
reason.dewormingFull: One deworming tablet (400 mg) on National Deworming Day. Next: {{next}}.
reason.anaemiaRecheck: The last Hb was {{hb}} g/dL, lower than normal. Repeat the test to see if treatment is working.
reason.anaemiaRefer: Hb {{hb}} g/dL is very low. See a doctor today.
reason.ifa_syrup: 1 ml iron syrup twice a week (6 months to 5 years).
reason.ifa_pink: One pink iron tablet once a week (5 to 9 years).
reason.ifa_blue: One blue iron tablet once a week (10 to 19 years).
reason.ifa_red_weekly: One red iron tablet once a week for women aged 20 to 49.
reason.ifaPostpartum: One red iron tablet every day for 6 months after delivery. Until {{until}}.
reason.calciumPostpartum: Calcium tablets for 6 months after delivery. Until {{until}}.
reason.bpScreen: Everyone aged 30 or more should have BP checked every year.
reason.sugarScreen: Everyone aged 30 or more should have blood sugar tested every year.
reason.oralScreen: A quick mouth check every 5 years from age 30.
reason.breastScreen: A breast check by a health worker every 5 years from age 30.
reason.cervicalScreen: A simple cervical cancer test every 5 years from age 30.
reason.underCare: You are already being treated for this. Keep your follow-up visits.

flag.pregnancyBpHigh: BP {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}} ({{on}}) is high for pregnancy. See a doctor today.
flag.pregnancyBpSevere: BP {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}} ({{on}}) is very high. Go to hospital now.
flag.highRiskPregnancy: This is a high-risk pregnancy. Plan the delivery at a hospital with a specialist.
flag.dangerSigns: Go to hospital at once if you notice any of these:
flag.anaemiaSevere: Hb {{hb}} g/dL ({{on}}): severe anaemia. See a doctor today.
flag.anaemiaFollowUpDue: A repeat Hb test is due.
flag.lowBirthWeight: Low birth weight ({{kg}} kg). Keep the baby warm skin-to-skin, breastfeed often and keep every ASHA visit.
flag.underweight: Weight is low for age (z-score {{z}}). Talk to the anganwadi worker about feeding.
flag.severeUnderweight: Weight is very low for age (z-score {{z}}). See a doctor soon.
flag.severeStunting: Height is very low for age (z-score {{z}}). See a doctor.
flag.muacSam: Arm size (MUAC) {{cm}} cm: severe acute malnutrition. See a doctor today.
flag.muacMam: Arm size (MUAC) {{cm}} cm: moderate malnutrition. The child needs extra food.
flag.growthFaltering: Weight has not gone up since {{since}} ({{from}} kg to {{to}} kg). Check feeding and illness.
flag.birthWeightNotRegained: The baby is still below birth weight ({{kg}} kg; born {{birthKg}} kg). See a doctor.
flag.bpHigh: BP {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}} ({{on}}) is high. See a doctor to confirm.
flag.bpVeryHigh: BP {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}} ({{on}}) is very high. See a doctor today.
flag.sugarHigh: Blood sugar {{mgdl}} mg/dL ({{on}}) is high. See a doctor for a confirmation test.
flag.screenAbnormal: The last {{kind}} ({{on}}) needs a doctor's follow-up.

danger.swelling: Swelling of the face or hands
danger.fetal_movement: The baby moves less or not at all

guideline.uncertain: Some numbers here are not yet confirmed
guideline.disclaimer: Based on national guidelines, not yet reviewed by a doctor for this app. A screening aid, not a diagnosis. Ask your health worker or doctor.
